statusText: Mapped policy state: BLOCK_NEW_BASE_ENTRIES. Current delayed NQ evidence shows renewed downside extension and holding near a fresh session low, with elevated rates, oil and weak semiconductor breadth acting as aligned amplifiers.
recommendation: Current Tail is in the elevated band. The immediate path remains vulnerable while NQ holds near fresh lows; later U.S. data and cash-open checkpoints can keep Tail elevated only if observed one-way continuation persists.
headline: NQ breaks lower and holds near the session low; Tail rises to the elevated band.
body: Delayed December NQ was 30,582.50, down 0.59%, with a 30,564.50-30,713.50 session range and price only about 18 points above the low. That is a materially weaker path than the prior assessment. Reuters also reported the U.S. 10-year yield near 5.12% and Brent above $102. Fresh Finviz context shows all seven tracked semiconductors negative on the latest session.

lookbackSummary: Tail was low through early September 23, rose into elevated territory during the U.S. selloff, then de-escalated as mean reversion returned. Overnight September 24 moved back to WATCH, and the current 07:00 UTC hour shows a renewed downside break sufficient to lift Tail back into the elevated band.
outlookSummary: Current downside structure is elevated rather than critical because fresh evidence shows a break and near-low holding but not yet a long sequence of failed retracements. The strongest later conditional window is 12:00-15:15 UTC around U.S. data, Fed remarks and the cash open; de-escalation requires meaningful two-way price discovery.

forecast.analysis: Delayed December NQ is 30,582.50, down 0.59%, only 18 points above a 30,564.50 session low after extending below the prior hour's range. Holding near the low, a 10-year yield around 5.12%, Brent above $102 and weak prior-session semiconductor breadth lift current Tail into the elevated band.
drivers: NQ is holding near a fresh session low after renewed downside extension
Fresh Finviz context shows all 7 tracked semiconductors negative on the latest session

forecast.analysis: John Williams speaks at 08:10 UTC. Tail remains elevated only if the already-weaker NQ structure continues to hold near new lows or extends with shallow rebounds; a meaningful recovery back through the broken range would lower the path risk.

After the Williams checkpoint, downside Tail stays elevated conditionally if NQ fails to reclaim the earlier overnight range and repeated selloffs hold near fresh extremes. A broad two-way recovery would argue for de-escalation.
drivers: Reclaim versus failure around the earlier overnight range

forecast.analysis: Late European morning is modeled back in WATCH if meaningful rotations reappear. A renewed low that persists without a material retracement would invalidate that de-escalation and return Tail to a blocking band.

Pre-U.S.-event positioning keeps Tail at the top of WATCH. The score does not assume a future directional break; it would rise only if the observed pre-release structure becomes one-way and cross-assets remain aligned.
drivers: No pre-release assumption of directional alignment
Rates and oil as cross-asset checkpoints

forecast.analysis: Jobless claims and BEA data at 12:30 UTC, followed by Hammack at 12:50, form the strongest pre-open catalyst cluster. Elevated Tail is conditional on observed post-release continuation with weak retracements.
drivers: Jobless claims and BEA release at 12:30 UTC

forecast.analysis: In the hour before the cash open, Tail is elevated if the data response keeps extending in one direction and retracements fail. Orderly price discovery or a sustained recovery from an extreme would pull the score lower.
drivers: Cross-asset alignment after the 12:30 UTC data

forecast.analysis: The U.S. cash open overlaps New Residential Sales at 14:00 UTC. High Tail requires an actual opening-auction continuation path with shallow pullbacks, repeated extension or session-extreme holding.

After the first cash-hour impulse, Tail remains elevated only if the market keeps extending and failed retracements confirm directional efficiency. A meaningful counter-move would reduce the probability of a pathological path.

Mid-session Tail stays elevated conditionally if the earlier U.S. impulse remains unresolved and NQ continues to hold near an extreme. Broader rotation back through the opening range would support a downgrade.

Later U.S. trade keeps a modest elevated Tail only if one-way structure persists. If volatility compresses and repeated rotations develop, mean-reversion evidence would strengthen and the score would fall toward WATCH.
drivers: Persistence of the U.S. directional move

forecast.analysis: Later U.S. trade keeps Tail elevated only if the earlier directional path remains persistent. Rates sensitivity can amplify an existing one-way NQ move, while a rates move without directional equity persistence mainly affects Stress.
drivers: Persistence of the earlier U.S. directional move
Rates response versus NQ price-path confirmation

forecast.analysis: Into the late U.S. session, Tail returns to WATCH if retracements have become meaningful. A fresh breakout that holds near an extreme with little giveback would keep the risk above that baseline.
Power-hour risk remains in WATCH unless the market shows renewed persistent extension. Two-way trade and recovery away from extremes would support further normalization.
Near the cash close, Tail stays in WATCH if closing flows remain rotational. A one-direction close pinned near the session extreme would preserve higher overnight path risk.
drivers: Close near extreme versus mean reversion

forecast.analysis: Early post-close conditions are modeled at the low end of WATCH if the U.S. session has not ended in a persistent extreme. Any unresolved one-way closing structure would keep risk higher than this baseline.
Late-evening Tail falls to low only if the earlier U.S. directional stress has dissipated and price discovery is balanced. The score is conditional, not an assumption that normalization will occur.

The overnight baseline is low Tail if volatility continues to decay and meaningful rotations persist. Renewed geopolitical or rates shocks that produce one-way NQ extension would invalidate that baseline.
During the quieter overnight hour, low Tail assumes no fresh persistent directional structure. A break that holds near a new extreme without retracement would raise path risk quickly.
Low Tail remains the conditional baseline if Asia-bound liquidity is balanced and no fresh catalyst creates directional efficiency. Cross-asset stress alone would not force a Tail escalation.
drivers: Cross-asset stress without assumed NQ continuation

forecast.analysis: As Asian liquidity deepens, Tail stays low provided rotations remain meaningful. A coordinated move in rates, oil and equity futures with shallow NQ pullbacks would be the escalation condition.
Approaching the European handoff, Tail moves to WATCH only conditionally on renewed directional pressure or unresolved overnight extremes. Stable two-way trade would keep the risk lower.

The European pre-open window carries modest WATCH risk if overnight structure remains directionally unresolved. A clean recovery through prior ranges would reduce Tail; fresh extension would increase it.
By the end of the 24-hour horizon, Tail remains WATCH conditionally if the market enters Europe with unresolved directional pressure. Balanced rotations would favor a lower score.
